replacement.method: every row dispatched against the real seeded CTMS ASGI app; expected_outputs.http_status is the OBSERVED status
replacement.previous_state: all 100 rows were synthesized filler targeting POST /api/ctms, which is not a route in this application
replacement.use_case_ids_renamed: the '_FILLER_' infix was removed from all 100 ids: the rows now carry real executed scenarios, so an id asserting filler was the last remaining untruth. tests/harness/requirements_matrix.json scenario_ids updated in the same change.

canonical_reconciliation.classification: DELETE-plus-write executed as an in-place rewrite, NOT an amendment. Per doctrine point 6 an amendment requires the business proposition to be unchanged; these rows carried NO proposition (empty body against the fabricated anchor POST /api/ctms, final_status SUCCESS asserted a priori), so each row's proposition was replaced wholesale. Recorded as such rather than claimed as an amendment.
canonical_reconciliation.no_rows_hard_deleted: Nothing was deleted, so the doctrine point 10 tombstone-with-retention obligation is not engaged for this change. The prior rows remain recoverable at origin/main:tests/harness/json_matrices/ctms_scenarios.json
canonical_reconciliation.static_discriminator_used: route-table existence (app.main.app.routes, 71 real API operations). No application code was added or changed to host a scenario -- the fabricated anchor POST /api/ctms was REMOVED and test_no_row_targets_a_route_that_does_not_exist now fails on any phantom path, which is the inverse of the eps /api/state-machine anti-pattern.
canonical_reconciliation.known_gap_assertion_strength: Assertions are http_status-only. Per doctrine point 4 a status-code assertion is not discriminating for audit/security/privacy requirements: the NFR-C-RE-001 (audit) and NFR-C-SE-001/002 (auth/RBAC) bindings are therefore NOT mutation-sensitive and are flagged requirement-unmet with defect references rather than counted as verified coverage. Strengthening these to discriminating body/side-effect assertions is queued, not done.

blocked_on_defect.doctrine: point 1 -- where the scenario and the requirement agree but the CODE disagrees, the CODE is the outlier: the expectation is NOT amended to observed behaviour.
blocked_on_defect.harness_contract: a row carrying blocked_on_defect is asserted to STILL FAIL; when the code starts satisfying it the harness fails and instructs removal of the flag, so a fix can never land silently.

deliberately_not_blocked.FR-C-62#2 (late SUSAR accepted, 200): FR-C-62 escalates past-deadline SUSARs rather than rejecting the report, so 200 is the REQUIRED behaviour
deliberately_not_blocked.FR-C-71#2 (shipment receipt accepted, 20: FR-C-71 requires receipt to be accepted and inventory incremented, so 200 is the REQUIRED behaviour

scenarios.title: DEFECT: an unrecognised visit status is accepted and stored verbatim
scenarios.description: FR-C-43 depends on visit status to distinguish missed from completed visits. PATCH with status 'not-a-real-status' returns 200 and the value is read back unchanged (proven by read-back), so status is not enum-validated. A missed visit can therefore be recorded as any string, defeating the missed-visit sweep and ProtocolDeviation creation this requirement mandates. Recorded expectation is the OBSERVED 200 and the row is tagged requirement-unmet: this documents the defect, it does not ratify it. EXPECTATION HELD AT 422, NOT the observed 200: the scenario and the requirement agree and the CODE is the outlier, so recording 200 would canonise the defect as the requirement. Marked blocked-on-defect CTMS-VAL-001; the harness asserts this row STILL fails and reports it the moment the code starts satisfying the requirement.

scenarios.title: DEFECT: eTMF completeness report is returned for a study that does not exist
scenarios.description: GET the eTMF report for absent study 999999 returns 200 with {'study_id':999999,'folders':[],'expired_count':0}. A caller cannot distinguish 'this study has no expired documents' from 'this study does not exist' -- the reading that matters for FR-C-52's expired-document flagging. The recruitment and safety reports share the defect; ip-accountability correctly returns 400, which is the control proving the guard is feasible. Recorded expectation is the OBSERVED 200, tagged requirement-unmet. EXPECTATION HELD AT 404, NOT the observed 200: the scenario and the requirement agree and the CODE is the outlier, so recording 200 would canonise the defect as the requirement. Marked blocked-on-defect CTMS-RPT-001; the harness asserts this row STILL fails and reports it the moment the code starts satisfying the requirement.
